anomalies.observed: On the Connections sheet, USB1 D- (pin 2) goes through R53 22 to net label USB_DP_FCC, while USB1 D+ (pin 3) goes through R52 22 to net label USB_DM_FCC. USB2 is wired the same way: D- to USB_DP_NAVC and D+ to USB_DM_NAVC.
anomalies.expected: USB D+ must connect to the MCU's USB_DP net and D- to USB_DM net. The FCC MCU (STM32H753) labels PA11 as USB_DM_FCC and PA12 as USB_DP_FCC; the NAVC MCU (STM32F405) similarly labels PA11 as USB_DM_NAVC and PA12 as USB_DP_NAVC. The spec calls for USB DFU programming/debug.

evidence.quote: Connections sheet: USB1 pin 2 (D-) → R53 22 → USB_DP_FCC; USB1 pin 3 (D+) → R52 22 → USB_DM_FCC
programming/debug via SWD, USB DFU, and UART-to-USB

anomalies.impact: Reversed USB data polarity on both programming/debug connectors prevents USB enumeration and DFU programming from working.

anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet, the feedback network around REG1 (MIC26903) has R5 6k8 from +5V to REG_FB, and both R4 19k6 and R6 1k3 connected from REG_FB to GND in parallel.
anomalies.expected: Only R5 and R6 should set the feedback divider; R4 should not be in parallel with R6. The schematic note and specification give Vout = 0.8*(1+R5/R6), which with R5=6.8k and R6=1.3k yields ≈5.0 V.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: 'R4 19k6' (connected between REG_FB and GND) and 'R6 1k3' (also between REG_FB and GND); note 'Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)'

anomalies.impact: The parallel combination of R4 (19.6k) and R6 (1.3k) gives an effective lower divider resistance of ~1.22k, raising the 5 V rail to about 5.26 V and potentially overstressing 5 V loads.

anomalies.observed: The INA219 current/voltage sensor (U1) on the Power sheet connects to I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC and has address pins A0/A1 tied to GND (address 0x40). The PCA9685 PWM driver (U2) on the FCC Peripherals sheet connects to the same I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC and has address pins A0–A5 tied to GND (address 0x40).
anomalies.expected: Two I2C devices on the same bus must have different addresses. The specification lists INA219 at 0x40 and PCA9685 at 0x40, so they must be placed on separate buses or one address must be changed.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: U1 INA219 pins 5/6 labeled I2C2_SCL_FCC and I2C2_SDA_FCC; pins 7/8 tied to GND. FCC Peripherals sheet: U2 PCA9685 pins 26/27 labeled I2C2_SCL_FCC and I2C2_SDA_FCC; pins 1–6 tied to GND.
Current/voltage sensor ... INA219AIDCNR, I2C addr 0x40; PWM/servo driver ... PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: I2C address conflict: both devices respond at 0x40 on the same bus, causing communication failures and unpredictable behavior when accessing either the current sensor or the PWM driver.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains three significant anomalies: USB D+/D- lines are swapped on both programming connectors, an extra resistor R4 in the buck feedback divider raises the 5 V rail to ~5.26 V, and the INA219 and PCA9685 share I2C2 at the same address 0x40.
